environment.description: Same NestJS microservice deployed on ECS Fargate. The ALB has an associated AWS WAFv2 WebACL with a custom rule group containing a regex pattern rule that inspects query string parameters for RFC 1918 and link-local address patterns (applied before the request reaches the application). Additionally, the ECS task runs with a network configuration where the bridge network mode uses a custom iptables FORWARD chain rule (applied via a sidecar init container with NET_ADMIN capability) that drops all outbound TCP SYN packets to 169.254.0.0/16 and 10.0.0.0/8 from the application container's network namespace. The ALB also injects a strict Content-Security-Policy response header via a Lambda@Edge-equivalent CloudFront distribution fronting the ALB: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'none'; style-src 'self'`.

config.network: VPC with iptables sidecar: iptables -A OUTPUT -d 169.254.0.0/16 -p tcp --syn -j DROP; iptables -A OUTPUT -d 10.0.0.0/8 -p tcp --syn -j DROP; iptables -A OUTPUT -d 172.16.0.0/12 -p tcp --syn -j DROP
config.waf: AWS WAFv2 WebACL with RegexPatternSet rule on QueryString matching (169\.254|10\.|192\.168|172\.(1[6-9]|2[0-9]|3[01])) in COUNT mode only (logging, not blocking)
config.cloudfront_function: Viewer response function adds Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'
config.metadata_service: IMDSv2 enforced (HttpTokens: required) on underlying host, but iptables rule blocks connectivity regardless
